annotationRationale: The main task is to extract function values from an identity over divisors. Prime factorization organizes the required inputs. The alternative verifies the suggested product formula using elementary finite geometric sums.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The substitutions correctly give \(f(1)=1\), \(f(7)=-6\), \(f(17)=f(289)=-16\), and \(f(119)=96\). All six divisors are included in the final identity, whose known terms sum to \(-95\), giving \(f(2023)=96\).

methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why only six inputs matter. Each substitution and the final arithmetic are explicit and reproducible without unfamiliar machinery.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For each prime power, the local divisor contribution is \((1-p)(1+p+\cdots+p^{e-1})+p^e=1\). Independent exponent choices therefore make the full divisor sum 1; the separate case \(n=1\) also holds. Recursive uniqueness identifies \(f(n)=\prod_{p\mid n}(1-p)\), giving 96.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE supplies the multiplicative-product idea. The candidate replaces its unexplained Dirichlet-convolution assertion with an elementary verification and accurately credits that source as third-party.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Uniqueness, the divisor-product expansion, and the geometric cancellation are explained. This is a complete accessible justification of the proposed formula.
